text: {"pass_id":"blind-hunt-c2","report_path":"scratch/lattice-c1/reports/blind-hunt-c2.md","verdict":"ADJUSTED","corrected_tier":"H","findings":[{"id":"c2-1","tier":"H","title":"_LockedConnection locks statements, not transactions; a concurrent cross-thread rollback on the shared connection silently discards another thread's uncommitted write, yielding a 202 custody ack without durable custody"},{"id":"c2-2","tier":"L","title":"initialize_cache_db only catches OperationalError on the schema-hash probe; a corrupt cache file raises DatabaseError, escapes, and the daemon fails to start instead of recreating the disposable cache"}],"refuted_subclaims":"Blind pass, no claim supplied. Internally refuted/downgraded: (a) Phase 8 doc claim that _LockedConnection makes the shared connection safe — REFUTED by Finding 1 (probe: thread A's row lost after thread B's IntegrityError rollback, A's commit returned normally). (b) execute_script's `with conn:` provides a migration transaction — REFUTED as a defect: executescript implicitly commits and runs in autocommit, but every durable migration and the cache schema use CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS with user_version/ schema_hash stamped last, so partial application reruns cleanly; not reportable. (c) cursor()/close() bypass the lock — REFUTED for reachability: no tree caller uses conn.cursor(); close() runs only after runtime.stop() drains executors.","added_mechanisms":"S1 [single-pass, same root as Finding 1] Shared-connection non-isolation: one connection = one transaction for all threads, so any thread's commit commits another thread's uncommitted multi-statement operation early and same-connection reads observe uncommitted writes; e.g. PeerRepository.add_block (INSERT blocks + UPDATE peers) can be seen half-applied by a concurrent reader and is non-atomic even without an exception. Severity M, same production population (request threadpool + 4 delivery + 2 maintenance workers). S2 [single-pass] docs/LOOSE_ENDS.md Phase 8's 'correct for v1' assertion is demonstrably false and must not be reused as evidence of correctness (doc-only).","fix_constraints":"Finding 1: repair must span the transaction, not the statement — acquire the RLock in Connection.__enter__ and release in __exit__ (reentrancy handles same-thread nesting), or use per-thread connections. Wrapping more statements in the existing per-statement lock does NOT fix it: commit/rollback are connection-global and can erase a peer thread's work. Escaping the structure-breaking (no cross-thread rollback) is not isolation with the check-then-act get_existing_receipt→create in InboundMessageService.accept; its UNIQUE catch is only safe once a rollback can no longer damage a peer. Finding 2: catch sqlite3.DatabaseError (base of OperationalError) around the hash probe and treat unreadable disposable cache as mismatch→recreate; handle failure to unlink/open as CacheError rather than an uncaught traceback.","unreachable":"Real multi-thread HTTP timing under uvicorn was not reproduced; the hit rate of the Finding 1 interleaving window is unproven (mechanism and trigger proven, frequency probabilistic). OS/filesystem behaviour producing cache corruption (Finding 2 trigger) was not exercised. uvicorn workers=1 is hardcoded, so multi-process sharing was not in scope; only in-process thread sharing."}

{"pass_id":"blind-hunt-g1","report_path":"scratch/lattice-c1/reports/blind-hunt-g1.md","verdict":"CONFIRMED","corrected_tier":"H","findings":[{"id":"G1-1","tier":"H","title":"Malformed operational certificate escapes WellKnownResolver.resolve_with_ip as SignatureError/ValueError, not ResolutionError (resolution.py:105-109); aborts _resolve_pending_senders batch permanently (runtime.py:914)"},{"id":"G1-2","tier":"M","title":"Resolve/pin path never enforces operational-certificate validity window (resolution.py:104-109); expired cert is pinned and keeps authenticating on the pin path"},{"id":"G1-S1","tier":"M","title":"Side discovery: _resolve_pending_senders never discards failed domains (docstring says it does), and cold-sender enqueue is unauthenticated with no cap -> unbounded retry loop and queue growth"}],"refuted_subclaims":"No claim was handed to this pass; the neutral question was checked against source. Sub-claims implicitly examined and REFUTED as defects: (a) address parsing permits scheme/host/userinfo injection into the fetch URL — refuted; parse_address rejects ':/@' in host and lowercases, and `?`/`#` cannot cross the doc.domain==domain equality; (b) pin key vs doc.domain vs fetched host can diverge by case — refuted; repository lowercases on both upsert and get; (c) pin() can persist a cert that fails verification — refuted; resolve() raises first, so upsert is unreachable; (d) accept-transfer can be replayed to re-bind a domain — refuted; after the move the old root no longer matches the pin; (e) resolved_ip is attacker-influenced — refuted; set by our own transport. G1-1 and G1-2 are not new discoveries: identical/the same family as hunt-g1#1 (CONFIRMED H by v-hunt-g1#1) and hunt-g1#2/hunt-e1#1/hunt-f2#1; re-derived independently, not copied.","added_mechanisms":"1) Cold-sender inbound domain enqueue is UNAUTHENTICATED: runtime.verify_inbound_message (runtime.py:638-651) returns (domain, True) for an unpinned domain BEFORE any signature check, and api.py:307 queues it before the rate limiter is reached — so the G1-1 starvation amplifier and the G1-S1 queue-growth fault need only a schema-valid POST /lattice/v1/messages, not a valid sender signature. 2) The escape also aborts daemon bootstrap (runtime.py:429 in start()) and yields unhandled 500s on the public messages route via _certificate_for_node (runtime.py:678) and on cli.py:579 / topology.py:224. 3) G1-S1 independently reproduced: failing domains remain in _unresolved_domains and are re-fetched every 30s tick (3 calls in 3 rounds).","fix_constraints":"A repair must make the whole cert-handling block fail closed into ResolutionError, not just wrap cert.verify: from_dict (line 105) raises ValueError and cert.verify raises SignatureError, both siblings of the caught IdentityError. Hardening runtime.py:914 alone fixes starvation but leaves the escape at bootstrap/500/cli/topology callers and leaves the hostile domain re-fetched. G1-S1 requires the loop to discard or time-bound failures AND a cap on the enqueue path; otherwise the resource fault persists. G1-2 cannot be fixed by an is_valid_at check at resolve_with_ip alone: certs expire after pinning, pins are never refreshed, so the check is needed at every consumption site (verify_message, verify_peer_card, _verify_against_well_known) or it merely converts acceptance into a permanent 401. No over-claim of key forgery: the exposed cert is covered by the attacker's own root signature, so custody pins are never poisoned.","unreachable":"No live daemon, DNS, or hostile network peer exercised — all three findings reproduced in-process with real Ed25519 keys, the real WellKnownResolver/RuntimeCoordinator methods, a fake transport/stub resolver; scheduler cadence and sorted-batch ordering read from source. Deployment fact (whether a real host keeps serving an expired well-known cert) unverifiable from tree. Exhaustive b64url_decode edge-case strictness not probed; only the four model-admitted cert mutations were exercised. transfer/reset handling examined via cli.cmd_trust_accept_transfer only; no live operator run."}

{"pass_id":"blind-hunt-d1","report_path":"scratch/lattice-c1/reports/blind-hunt-d1.md","verdict":"CONFIRMED","corrected_tier":"H","findings":[{"id":"blind-hunt-d1#1","tier":"H","title":"3xx redirects re-enter urllib3 with no policy re-validation (GATED behind hunt-b1b#1)"},{"id":"blind-hunt-d1#2","tier":"M","title":"IPv6 destinations build an unbracketed URL; every IPv6-first/literal transport call fails (PRODUCTION, not gated)"},{"id":"blind-hunt-d1#3","tier":"M","title":"Unanchored private_suffixes endswith admits lookalike registrable domains (LATENT)"},{"id":"blind-hunt-d1#4","tier":"L","title":"Daemon direct NetworkPolicy construction skips suffix normalization; uppercase/trailing-dot suffixes fail closed (LATENT)"},{"id":"blind-hunt-d1#5","tier":"S-","title":"Public mode does not reject CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10 (and multicast)"}],"refuted_subclaims":"1) \"the classmethod strips the operator's dot, widening the private-mode bypass\" — REFUTED: NetworkPolicy.private() is called only by tests/CLI; the daemon constructs NetworkPolicy directly at runtime.py:203, so s.lower().strip(\".\") never runs in production, and a leading-dot suffix anchors correctly there. 2) redirect reaches \"any address\" including cross-host HTTPS — NARROWED/REFUTED: the retained assert_hostname blocks a different-host HTTPS redirect; the working arm is the http:// scheme downgrade / TLS-less target. 3) redirect surfaces the well-known GET response body as the federation response — REFUTED for the discovery path: resolution.py:50-92 validates status, content-type, JSON, domain, node ID, and signatures, so that path is blind SSRF (request emitted, body discarded); the body IS consumed on the POST delivery/gossip paths. 4) IPv6-literal host follows the same unbracketed-URL mechanism — REFUTED as the same mechanism: parse_url retains brackets (\"[::1]\"), so getaddrinfo raises gaierror (\"DNS resolution failed\"); distinct sub-mechanism, still a failure. 5) CGNAT finding's claimed outcome (connect/forward/process internal response) — REFUTED: blocked by TLS hostname pinning and, for any live connection, by the known gate; S- retained on mechanism only.","added_mechanisms":"1) Empty-suffix fail-open: NetworkPolicy(mode=\"private\", private_suffixes=(\"\",)) admits EVERY hostname (\"\".endswith is True); config.py rejects an empty list but not an empty element; classmethod suffixes=[\".\"] normalizes to (\"\",) and fails open identically. Anchoring alone does not close it. 2) in_suffix short-circuits the IP check entirely (guard \"if not in_cidr and not in_suffix\"), so a suffix-matched host may resolve to loopback/link-local/RFC1918 and still be admitted; harm bounded by TLS hostname pinning. 3) Same lookalike fetch reachable from the public gossip route (topology.verify_candidate). 4) Host header (original hostname) is retained across a redirect; urllib3 strips only Authorization by default, so an internal target sees the attacker's Host. 5) Outbound response body is unbounded: preload_content=True with no size cap, response.data fed straight to strict_json_loads. 6) Private CA bundle is additive to the default system CA store (create_default_context + load_verify_locations), so private mode with private_ca_path still accepts publicly-trusted certs.","fix_constraints":"Redirect repair MUST NOT ship the SSRF: set redirect=False / Retry(redirect=False) or intercept Location and re-run the same single-resolution connect-to-validated-IP discipline; re-check the https-only invariant on the Location (the http:// downgrade is unaffected by assert_hostname, which does not apply to HTTP pools); strip/replace the forwarded Host and do not forward the POST body across origins. IPv6 repair: bracket IPv6 literals when formatting target_url (ipaddress objects format unbracketed) and handle bracketed hosts from parse_url before getaddrinfo; this survives a hunt-b1b#1 repair. Suffix repair: anchor at a DNS label boundary (host == s or host.endswith(\".\"+s)) in BOTH validate_ip and hostname_allowed, and reject empty/whitespace/dot-only suffixes in NetworkConfig and NetworkPolicy.__post_init__ (empty suffix fail-opens the whole policy); normalize consistently across the daemon's direct construction (runtime.py:203) and NetworkPolicy.private(), since the classmethod is off the production path. CGNAT/incomplete-range repair: consider rejecting not ip.is_global in public mode rather than enumerating flags, so 100.64/10 and future gaps are covered.","unreachable":"Gated claims (finding 1, SD2) cannot be exercised through the daemon today: the known fields/assert_hostname call-shape defect makes every urlopen raise before a response; redirect behaviour was read from pinned urllib3 2.7.0 source (poolmanager.py:486), not re-run end to end. Provider/upstream behaviour (real AAAA-first resolver ordering for a given peer, attacker registrability of a publicly-trusted tail-lookalike cert, cloud-metadata/CGNAT deployment topologies) is outside the tree and unverified. Deployed population (private mode vs public, CGNAT) is unverifiable in-tree and is exactly why findings 3/4/SD1/5 are LATENT. Enumeration is identifier/literal rg; a dynamically introduced redirect control or policy call outside the named symbols would not match (none exists in-tree)."}

{"pass_id":"blind-hunt-k1","report_path":"scratch/lattice-c1/reports/blind-hunt-k1.md","verdict":"CONFIRMED","corrected_tier":"M","findings":[{"id":"blind-hunt-k1#1","tier":"M","title":"Shipped systemd ExecStart cannot start the daemon: top-level --config after the subcommand is rejected by the CLI parser (exit 2)"},{"id":"blind-hunt-k1#2","tier":"L","title":"ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP kills the uvicorn daemon; Restart=on-failure does not restart (SIGHUP is a clean exit)"}],"refuted_subclaims":"Both findings coincide with the existing corpus report hunt-k1.md (#1/#2) on the identical scope; passes were blind, both were re-derived independently. Sub-claims refuted or corrected: (1) The overbroad sweep \"every documented lattice init/upgrade/status/keys rotate-operational invocation fails\" is REFUTED IN PART — docs/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md:19 (init) and :47 (rotate-operational) omit --config and parse/run fine; only documented commands that PASS --config after the subcommand fail. (2) Finding #2 frequency corrected: hunt-k1#2 reported M with frequency \"plausible in normal operation\"; the trigger population is operators who use the advertised `systemctl reload` (docs instruct `systemctl restart`, not reload) and this tree grounds no normal-operation cadence for it, so per the pinned calibration rule the frequency is LATENT and the tier is corrected M→L (mechanism upheld; outage is real but recovery is one manual start). (3) No other sub-claim refuted: mechanism (argparse top-level-only --config; serve subparser declares only --state-dir/--cache-dir/--log-level), trigger (deploy/lattice.service:26 ExecStart string), and deterministic frequency of #1 all hold and were verified by direct execution of the repo venv console script.","added_mechanisms":"On the X-Forwarded-For side-discovery trace (out-of-scope file set, api/rate-limit pass): (A) the rate-limit key space is unbounded — nginx appends to client-supplied XFF and api._peer_ip takes the first entry, so spoofed keys are unlimited; (B) RateLimiter._buckets (rate_limit.py:82,88-99) is never evicted, each new key inserts two TokenBuckets, and runtime.py:500-501 persists them, so spoofed keys cause unbounded in-memory and cache-DB growth (H-adjacent amplifier). (C) docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:81 claims Nginx \"owns ... IP rate limits\" while deploy/lattice.nginx.conf defines no limit_req_zone/limit_req (LOOSE_ENDS Phase 9 already admits it) — docs-vs-config inconsistency, no runtime trigger, recorded as a design risk not a finding.","fix_constraints":"Finding #1: a unit-line-only fix is insufficient — docs/LATTICE_SYSTEMD.md (4 sites), docs/MIGRATIONS.md:15, and README.md:22 carry the same post-subcommand order and re-seed it; tests/test_deployment.py:77 asserts the broken string verbatim, so the unit change must also update that assertion or the test pins the defect. Structural fix: make --config a global option accepted on both sides of the subcommand (parents= reuse) rather than merely reordering the token. Note serve without --config already defaults to /etc/lattice/config.toml. Finding #2: do not add an ExecReload that sends a signal uvicorn does not handle; either implement a SIGHUP reload path in cmd_serve or remove ExecReload and document `systemctl restart` (must also not rely on Restart=on-failure to recover, since SIGHUP death is a clean exit). Side-discovery fix: trust only the unspoofable X-Real-IP (or the right-most XFF entry) AND add a bucket cap/TTL with eviction — an XFF-parsing fix alone leaves the unbounded bucket_map.","unreachable":"No live systemd or Nginx on this macOS host: systemd-analyze verify, actual LoadCredentialEncrypted decrypt/chown semantics, StateDirectory ownership repair of pre-existing files, and the nginx -t test (skipped when nginx is absent) were not executed. Finding #2's decisive systemd consequence (death-by-SIGHUP is a clean exit for Restart=on-failure, so no restart) rests on documented systemd.service(5) semantics web-verified from multiple sources, not reproduced; its core mechanism (SIGHUP terminates uvicorn) is source-verified. Finding #1's secondary \"unit latches to failed within ~30s\" is not reproduced; its core failure site (argparse exit 2) is execution-verified and systemd-independent. The deployed /opt/lattice/venv/bin/lattice path does not exist here; wrapper inferred from the equivalent repo-venv console script. Fresh wheel built from a byte-identical /tmp copy (write authority forbids in-tree builds); version string differs (fallback 0.1.0.dev0), content unaffected. tests/test_wheel.py read, not executed (would write into repo dist/)."}

{"pass_id":"v-hunt-k1#2","report_path":"scratch/lattice-c1/reports/v-hunt-k1#2.md","verdict":"ADJUSTED","corrected_tier":"M","refuted_subclaims":"REFUTED: the claim's \"Reachability: PRODUCTION (operator action)\" is not an unconditional production path — it is GATED behind hunt-k1#1 (deploy/lattice.service:26 ExecStart fails argparse: `.venv/bin/lattice serve --config ...` -> \"unrecognized arguments\", exit 2). No live daemon exists under the shipped unit, and systemd refuses `reload` on an inactive unit, so the SIGHUP path is unreachable today; it becomes live only when #1 is repaired. Partially corrected (not refuted): the claim labels the systemd restart-suppression as \"the only unproven component resting on documented semantics\" — I strengthened it to traced at systemd C-source level (is_clean_exit(...,EXIT_CLEAN_DAEMON) -> SERVICE_SUCCESS for SIGHUP; service_shall_restart ON_FAILURE returns !IN_SET(result, SUCCESS,...) = false). Frequency sub-claim: the claim's own \"cadence is whatever the operator's reload habit is. Not automatic.\" is accurate — operator-driven, no code/documentation invokes `systemctl reload lattice` (docs use `systemctl restart lattice`), so cadence is ungrounded; flagged, not DEMONSTRATED.","added_mechanisms":"1) `systemctl reload-or-restart lattice` also triggers the kill, because `ExecReload` exists so the \"safe\" verb resolves to reload (SIGHUP) rather than restart — widens the operator population. 2) The reload capability is unimplemented, not merely mishandled: `rg 'SIGHUP|reload' lattice/` finds no config hot-reload path, so even a SIGHUP-surviving daemon would not re-read config.toml; `ExecReload` promises a capability absent from the code. 3) Earlier failure site on the same unit trace: line 26 (`hunt-k1#1`) fires before line 27 is ever reached in a real deployment. 4) No network-peer reachability: the trigger is operator/systemd only; no HTTP input can cause or avoid it.","fix_constraints":"Removing `ExecReload` restores Restart=on-failure semantics but silently drops the advertised reload capability; if reload is intended, add a real SIGHUP handler (or Type=notify-reload with RELOADING=1/READY=1) AND a config-reload path (none exists). Do NOT fix via `Restart=always` — that masks genuine clean-exit bugs and converts a crash-loop into a restart-loop; the defect is the unhandled reload signal. Fix #1 and #2 together: once ExecStart parses, the first advertised reload kills a healthy node with no self-recovery. Restart=on-failure + StartLimitBurst=3/StartLimitInterval=60 interacts with #1's restart-retry. `tests/test_deployment.py` asserts nothing about ExecReload/SIGHUP, so the suite neither pins nor catches a regression. A repair that only escapes the kill (e.g. dropping the reload verb) is not the same as restoring a working reload; the two must be decided deliberately.","unreachable":"No live systemd on this macOS host: the restart-suppression half is traced against systemd main `src/core/service.c` (is_clean_exit / service_shall_restart / SERVICE_RELOAD -> service_enter_running -> service_enter_exited_or_stop path), not exercised against a running PID 1. No live deployment of the shipped unit is possible (it cannot start — hunt-k1#1), so the gated call rests on #1's verified parse failure plus systemd's refusal to reload an inactive unit. A deployment drop-in setting RestartForceExitStatus=/SuccessExitStatus= (absent from this tree) could alter the restart decision. The /opt/lattice/venv interpreter and $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY were not exercised (irrelevant to the signal path). Nothing in the tree was modified.","findings":[{"id":"hunt-k1#2","tier":"M","title":"ExecReload sends SIGHUP, which terminates the uvicorn daemon (exit 129); Restart=on-failure does not restart it (clean signal) — mechanism/trigger confirmed, reachability corrected to gated behind hunt-k1#1"}]}

{"pass_id":"blind-hunt-a1","report_path":"scratch/lattice-c1/reports/blind-hunt-a1.md","verdict":"CONFIRMED","corrected_tier":"H","refuted_subclaims":"Refuted while checking the route contracts: (1) \"202 without custody is a defect\" — the BlockedSenderError/CustodyError paths return a signature-valid rejected receipt at 202, which PROTOCOL §8 explicitly defines as final; not reported. (2) \"gossip verification must be rate-limited first\" — PROTOCOL §5.2 requires verifying the first card to derive the identity key, so verify-before-limit is spec-mandated; not reported. (3) \"blocking synchronous calls in request handlers are a defect\" — synchronous core is invariant 4; not reported. (4) \"the missing 403 entry in _STATUS_PROBLEM_MAP is a live mis-map\" — no HTTPException(403) is raised on any path, so the gap is unreachable today; recorded clean. (5) \"all errors map to RFC 9457\" — largely true; only the ValueError escape paths (Finding 1) break it.","added_mechanisms":"1. Same AddressError-escape class has a second site: api.py:322 _extract_domain_from_address(to_address) is uncaught and fires after signature verification, so an authenticated pinned peer with a malformed to_address also gets a plain-text 500 (reproduced). 2. Finding 2's spoofed XFF feeds rate_limit.py:RateLimiter._bucket, which never evicts and is persisted/restored via runtime _persist_rate_limits; unbounded memory and cache-DB row growth, reproducible (7 buckets after 6 distinct XFF). 3. Recipient-ownership check at api.py:322-323 is bypassed for canonical addresses (domain==None -> \\\"\\\"), so a message addressed to another node's canonical ID is accepted with a 202 \\\"accepted\\\" receipt and custody, contra PROTOCOL §7 (reproduced; priced as side discovery L).","fix_constraints":"A repair for Finding 1 must wrap every parse_address call on the inbound path (both runtime.verify_inbound_message's from_address parse and api._extract_domain_from_address) or validate address format in the Message model, and must map to a 400 Problem Detail (LATTICE_INVALID_ADDRESS) rather than 401/500 — catching only RuntimeError is insufficient because AddressError is a ValueError. The from_address site is reachable pre-authentication, so it must not depend on sender resolution. A repair for Finding 2 must derive the peer IP from a value the edge actually controls (rightmost XFF added by the trusted proxy, or X-Real-IP), not the client-supplied leftmost token. Fixing Finding 2 does NOT fix Finding 3: node-ID buckets remain attacker-mintable via self-signed first cards, so the limiter needs eviction/TTL or a cardinality cap independent of the IP fix. Finding 4 needs an explicit 415/400 on unsupported/missing version in Content-Type/Accept; FastAPI's incidental rejection of non-JSON media types is not sufficient and does not cover the version parameter.","unreachable":"Bounds: (a) nginx edge behavior assumed from the in-tree deploy/lattice.nginx.conf ($proxy_add_x_forwarded_for, no limit_req/limit_conn); a deployment that strips client XFF or adds edge rate limiting would reduce Finding 3's magnitude (not its mechanism), so Finding 3 magnitude is SUSPECTED, mechanism DEMONSTRATED. (b) The actual memory-per-bucket and sustained request throughput needed for OOM were not measured; growth is linear in distinct attacker-chosen peer_ids and persists to the cache DB. (c) Live provider/upstream strictness and real federated peer behavior were not exercised; no external network or daemon was started. (d) Findings 1–4 were reproduced with in-process TestClient against the real RuntimeCoordinator, not against the deployed nginx/TLS edge, so header-forwarding behavior for Finding 2 is verified only against the checked-in edge config, not a running edge.","findings":[{"id":"F1","tier":"M","title":"Unauthenticated malformed from_address raises AddressError out of verify_inbound_message -> plain-text HTTP 500 (second authenticated to_address site)"},{"id":"F2","tier":"M","title":"_peer_ip trusts client-controlled leftmost X-Forwarded-For -> IP-fallback gossip rate limit bypassable"},{"id":"F3","tier":"H","title":"RateLimiter._buckets never evicted and keyed by attacker-controlled peer_id -> unbounded memory and cache-DB growth"},{"id":"F4","tier":"L","title":"Public routes do not enforce the versioned media type (PROTOCOL 11 MUST)"}]}

{"pass_id":"blind-hunt-c1","report_path":"scratch/lattice-c1/reports/blind-hunt-c1.md","verdict":"CONFIRMED","corrected_tier":"M","refuted_subclaims":"Refuted after re-derivation: (1) SQL injection / unvalidated column construction in PeerRepository.transition_peer — the only dynamic SQL builds fixed literal column fragments from a closed {verified,established,blocked} map and binds all values as parameters; no caller identifier reaches SQL. (2) Repository/schema column mismatch — every INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE column exists in durable/001_initial.sql or cache_schema.sql. (3) FK violation on custody create due to missing root history — ensure_root_history precedes create in both OutboundMessageService.submit and InboundMessageService.accept, and foreign_keys=ON. (4) claim_pending/claim_for_webhook same-second double-return of a leased row — not reachable: the recurring task cadence (10s) exceeds the 1s timestamp resolution and all rows in a returned batch are marked terminal/released synchronously before the next claim. (5) remove_block leaving peers.state='blocked' — intended per BlockStore.unblock docstring; enforcement keys on the blocks table, not peers.state. (6) Migration runner's newer-than-target refusal, integrity/FK prechecks, per-script user_version verification, and idempotency are correct.","added_mechanisms":"F1 (M): shared single SQLite connection (connection.py:_LockedConnection, open_connection factory+check_same_thread=False) with an RLock that wraps only individual execute/commit/rollback calls, not the transaction spanning a repository method's 'with self._conn:' block. A concurrent thread whose repository write raises calls the overridden rollback() and discards another thread's not-yet-committed DML; the other method's commit is then a no-op and it returns success. Reproduced at repository level (a contacts row inserted by thread B and reported successful persisted as [] after thread A's simulated IntegrityError rollback). Remotely forceable via duplicate message_id from a different node. F2 (M): migrations.py:_backup_path/migrate copy only the main DB file via shutil.copy2 while the WAL connection is open; reproduced with the real migrate — the pre-migration backup lacks committed data (even its schema) because pages live in <db>-wal. F3 (L, latent): execute_script uses executescript, which auto-commits; a failed migration leaves partial DDL with user_version unchanged (reproduced) — benign today only because 001 is IF NOT EXISTS-idempotent. Side (S1) runtime.py:803-824 raw cache_conn.execute writes never committed in-block; (S2) build/dist contain durable/002 (user_version=2) absent from source, so a v2 DB is refused by migrate (out of scope per invariant 8); (S3) no v2 fixture despite docs.","fix_constraints":"F1: a repair must make the whole transaction scope mutually exclusive per connection (thread-local connections or a small pool), not merely widen the per-call RLock; it must preserve the reentrancy that nested repository calls (transition_peer/upsert_peer call get_peer inside 'with self._conn:') and the BaseRepository.connect path rely on, and it must also cover raw conn.execute callers (runtime circuit-breaker writes). F2: a correct backup must checkpoint the WAL or use the SQLite backup API / VACUUM INTO under a consistent view; copying -wal/-shm alone is racy against live writers, and the backup name/hash (main-file-bytes only) can collide across WAL states and be silently reused. F3: each migration must be wrapped in an explicit BEGIN/COMMIT (executescript cannot be made atomic by 'with conn:' alone); a repair must also decide rollback-on-failure so user_version and schema never diverge. Escaping structure-breaking is not the concern here (SQL is already parameterized); the repairs concern transaction scope and snapshot consistency.","unreachable":"Could not confirm whether durable schema v2 (002_staging_and_erasure.sql, present in build/lib and every dist wheel 2026-08-01..2026-09-27) was ever a released schema rather than a build artifact; treated as out-of-scope per invariant 8 and recorded as S2. Did not run a live daemon or instrument a real deployment, so the collision RATE for Finding 1 is unmeasured (mechanism reproduced deterministically; rate SUSPECTED). WAL/checkpoint behaviour exercised on macOS/Python 3.12 only; the deployment target's filesystem is unverified.
